issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) require a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This adds an unexpected parameter and changes the intended signature, causing a mismatch between the specification and the provided reference implementation that could confuse students and break any expected tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specification by changing the solution's method signature to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters and returning the total number of students (inscribed + guest). Update any internal calls in the solution (e.g., getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to call the no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents(). Alternatively, if the boolean parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, UML and template to document and require getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) instead.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the method signature for the same conceptual operation (returning total students) and forces callers (and students) to reason about an extra parameter not present in the specification or template TODOs, creating a mapping mismatch between the exercise description and the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by implementing a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (inscribed + guest). If optional behavior to exclude guests is desired, add a clearly named overload or a separate method (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) or getInscribedNumberOfStudents()) and update the UML/problem statement to document the alternative explicitly.
